a RELEASED tag on the public mirror cannot be silently MOVED. scripts/publish-public.sh force-pushed the tag (:286) while pushing main NON-force (:285) -- the commit history was protected from rewrite while the TAG, the only name an adopter ever pins to, could be moved out from under them. Now: publish_decision() is a PURE function encoding a PRECISE rule (tag absent -> publish; tag published + tree IDENTICAL -> noop, so the benign idempotent re-run STAYS GREEN and the gate never fires on the happy path; tag published + tree DIFFERS -> REFUSE, which is the actual defect: every adopter pinned to that tag would silently receive a tree they never audited). Underneath it, -f/--force are gone: a NON-FORCE tag push is rejected by git itself if it would MOVE a ref, which is the layer that still holds if a concurrent publish lands the tag between our clone and our push (the TOCTOU window the refusal alone cannot close). PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: the selftest exercises a REAL local repo (no network, no creds) -- a non-force tag push REFUSES to move a published tag, AND --force DOES move it, so the first result is load-bearing rather than vacuous. HONEST CEILING: this binds the TOOL, the accident, and the agent. It does NOT bind a human with push rights doing `git push --force` by hand -- only a forge-side tag ruleset does (see mirror-tag-protection), and a repo ADMIN CAN LIFT THAT RULESET. Immutability is ENFORCED BY THE FORGE and merely ATTESTED here; we claim tamper-EVIDENT-and-deliberate, never tamper-proof.

a release that is merged and TAGGED but never PUBLISHED is DETECTED, not silent. Publication is a purely MANUAL maintainer act (ci.yml only --selftests publish-public.sh), so the mirror carried ONE commit and ONE tag (v3.122.0) while the kit was at 3.134.0 -- TWELVE releases, incl. EIGHT guard/control-plane commits (CP-9, CP-10, DRIFT-1, DRIFT-2), unpublished; it grew from 9 to 12 unnoticed. The staleness was not the defect, the SILENCE was. conformance/mirror-current.sh compares the released VERSION against the mirror's published tags and turns RED when the mirror is behind. It is a CRON check (drift-watch.yml), NOT a PR gate -- the same constraint that shaped release-tagged.sh: publication happens AFTER the merge and AFTER the tag, so a PR-time gate would be RED on EVERY merge, and a gate that cries wolf on the happy path gets ignored and is then worth nothing when it fires for real. Honest ceiling: up to 7 days to notice. The mirror URL is SINGLE-SOURCED from publish-public.sh's PUBLIC_REMOTE_DEFAULT and FAILS CLOSED if that line is absent -- never a guessed default, because a currency check aimed at the WRONG remote is worse than no check (it would report a confident green about a repo nobody publishes to). Non-vacuous (local git repos as remotes; no network, no creds): current -> GREEN; behind -> RED; ZERO tags -> RED (not a vacuous pass); UNREACHABLE -> exit 2 UNVERIFIED, never a pass (absence of evidence is not evidence of currency); single source stripped -> FAIL closed. HONEST CEILING: it proves a TAG EXISTS on the mirror -- NOT that the mirror's TREE equals the kit's export at that version (that equality is verified by publish-public.sh AT PUBLISH TIME). It answers exactly one question: did the publish ever happen? Green means the mirror is CURRENT, not that it is GOOD. Detection, not automation: publication stays human-commanded.

the DESIGN GATE is CHECKED (whether it is BOUND as a required context is repo configuration and is NOT verified here — UNBOUND, this gate is ADVISORY and blocks nothing; and even bound it is bypassed by an admin merge where enforce_admins is false) for Sensitive/Control-plane change-sets: a GO record in refs/notes/promotions must carry BOTH `gate: design` AND a `scope:` line equal to one of THIS change's keys, and a record scoped elsewhere satisfies NEITHER: CI matches TWO keys — the caller-supplied PR key (`--scope PR-<n>`) OR the branch key (`scope: branch/<head-branch>`, from `--head-branch`, owner ruling D11 — which is what lets a design GO bind before a PR exists, and since 2026-08-11 satisfy the merge gate with NO re-record, retiring the [S4]#7 interim protocol); the `--pre-push` hook mode DERIVES the branch key alone and is still NOT satisfied by a PR-scoped record. A head-branch name outside the D11 charset is author-controlled input that no record could carry, so it DROPS the branch key, DISCLOSES the drop on stderr and leaves the rc unchanged — it is never a refusal. There is NO any-scope mode: one was built and WITHDRAWN, because on a ledger holding a single surviving design record it is permanently green (measured — one slice's GO satisfied another slice's push). ALSO REQUIRED since 2026-08-11 (D-240811-3, the ceiling for permanent branch-scoped records): CONTAINMENT IN TWO LEGS — the approved-sha must be an ANCESTOR of the graded head AND NOT an ancestor of merge-base(graded head, base), so a record left by a historic branch of the same reusable name is inert; the reachability leg ALONE is not enough and that was measured (once the historic branch is merged or rebased into the base its approved commit is on the mainline, so a new branch of the same name inherits it reachably and the record satisfied unrelated work at rc 0). The base is named by --base-ref (CI passes github.base_ref) or derived from the local default branch; where NO base resolves, or the resolved base already contains the graded head, leg 2 is SKIPPED with a DISCLOSED one-line degradation, the rc is UNCHANGED and the verdict downgrades to `containment: reachable-only` — so a green from such a run carries the reachability half and NOT the not-already-integrated half. A matching record that fails either leg is DEFECTIVE with a named reason (including a GO recorded at the FORK POINT, approved-sha == the merge-base), and a valid sibling still carries. NOT claimed: that containment is an ORDERING claim (it is not — see below), that leg 2 ran on every clone shape (it is base-dependent and discloses when it did not), and not that a fork PR cannot reproduce a branch name plus a public commit; it can, and the merge control there is the owner-only ratification approval, not this gate. The judgment-surface render is SINGLE-SOURCED here as `--render` and INVOKED by both workflow legs (locked by adopter-gates-parity.sh), so the render's scope keys cannot drift from the gate's. It must name an approver as `<id> [<label of the derived form>]` with [self-asserted] refused at control-plane, and must carry an `approved-sha:` that is a HEX OBJECT NAME (not a revision expression like HEAD, which would re-resolve at check time and bind nothing) resolving to a commit that TOUCHES the artifact; and `basis:` must match CB_DESIGN_GLOB (default `docs/architecture/*-design.md`) and be tracked, non-symlink and non-placeholder — unconstrained, a repo with ZERO design documents passed by naming README.md. Ordinary derives N-A. TWO ARMS SINCE 2026-08-15 (C8): a PURE governance-record change (a meta-control panel sitting + its bookkeeping) has no design of its own, and the three shipped PRs that hit that gap all answered it with the same workaround — point `basis:` at a design doc the commit happens to amend — so the class is CLOSED rather than routinised. Such a change records `--gate governance` with a CB_GOV_GLOB (default `docs/architecture/*-meta-control-*.md`) basis and is adjudicated by THE SAME chain with exactly two deltas: the basis glob, and a GOVERNANCE DIFF-SHAPE GUARD requiring the change's cumulative file list — consumed from `promotion-readiness.sh --changed-files`, the single derivation authority, NEVER a local git diff — to be a SUBSET of an enumerated governance set (BACKLOG.md · the meta-control glob · docs/governance/DECISIONS.md · docs/governance/.meta-control-last · docs/governance/meta-control-log.md · docs/kit-internals/meta-control.md · skills/*/SKILL.md · CB_DESIGN_GLOB). So the governance pass is earned by a DERIVED property of the diff, never by an author's declaration; an escaping path is rc 2 with the path NAMED and the cure stated (split the cures, or record a design GO for the payload), and an UNDERIVABLE change-set is rc 2 FAIL-CLOSED naming the fetch-depth: 0 cure (the containment-leg-2 disclosed-skip precedent deliberately does NOT transfer — this guard is the arm's only anti-laundering leg). A record carrying BOTH accepted gate values is DEFECTIVE by disqualification, never dispatched to an arm by matcher order. `scripts/promotion-verify.sh` is UNCHANGED (--gate is free text there). The DESIGN arm is byte-unchanged, so the live defective record `1d9f0afa` (design gate + meta-control basis) STAYS defective and is replayed byte-faithfully as a durable selftest leg. NOT claimed by the governance arm: any binding of the panel artifact's CONTENT to the change (the same content-binding ceiling the design arm carries — the owner's read at the sitting is the content control, D-240805-4); and the governance set is an ENUMERATION, so a new legitimate governance surface REDS until it is added (over-tight is loud, over-wide is green-while-dark; boarded as GOVERNANCE-SET-FAMILY-LOCK). A MIXED PR (governance record + routed control-plane cures) still needs a design basis for its payload — that is the gate being right, not a gap. ⚠️ MAKES NO ORDERING CLAIM: the ordering predicate was WITHDRAWN after five defeats in three adversarial rounds (reflexive ancestor; a sixth derivation site; touch-not-authorship; a relocated stale anchor; abbreviated-SHA false REDs) — the design may have been written AFTER the work, and nothing here detects that (boarded: CEREMONY-ORDERING-PROOF). Also NOT proven: authorship (a zero-byte create satisfies a touch), quality, that anyone read it (PR #430 would pass), or tamper-resistance — a note BINDS but does not AUTHENTICATE and refs/notes/* is outside branch protection. EXIT CONTRACT (breaking for anyone who wired this script into their own CI): 0 = pass or N-A; 1 = WAITING, reserved for the single state "no GO record scoped to this change exists yet", which CI renders yellow and still blocking; 2 = ANOMALY — a scoped GO that exists and is DEFECTIVE, or a gate that could not evaluate. Red is therefore reserved for something genuinely broken, and a defect can never render as the waiting state; the selftest's negative-leg helper defaults its expected rc to 2, so any refusal THAT HAS A NEGATIVE LEG fails the suite if it is left at 1 — a new refusal with no leg at all is not covered by this, and the exit contract in the script header states the standing rule for that case
